And yet there’s another way to satisfy this want. We learn to prize the things of the spirit, to long for revelation which nowhere burns more nobly and with greater beauty than in the New Testament. I must open that fundamental text; I must, now, with all honorable dedication, turn that holy original into my beloved German.

@@U00307@@
(He opens a large volume and prepares to begin.)

@@U00308@@
It is written: “In the beginning was the Word!” Already I’m stuck. Who will help me? Who? Someone! How can I rate the Word so highly? I must translate it otherwise if ’'m truly enlightened by the spirit. It is written: “In the beginning was the Mind!” Not so fast. Let’s not rush over that first line! Is it truly the mind that creates all things? Surely it ought to read: “In the beginning was the Force!” And yet I’ve scarcely written it and immediately something tells me it’s not right. But, yes, now the spirit’s helping, helping me, and all at once I have it, and write:
translation:
@@U00306@@
然而还有另一种方法可以满足这种需求。我们学会珍视精神的事物，渴望得到新约中最崇高、最美丽的启示。我必须打开那篇基础文本；现在，我必须以所有光荣的奉献精神，将这神圣的原作变成我心爱的德语。

@@U00307@@
（他打开一本大书，准备开始。）

@@U00308@@
经上记着：“太初有道！”我已经被困住了。谁来帮助我？ WHO？有人！我怎么能对神的话语给予如此高的评价呢？如果我真的受到精神的启发，我必须翻译它。经上写道：“太初有心！”没那么快。我们不要急于完成第一行！真的是心创造了万物吗？当然，它应该是：“太初是原力！”然而我刚写完，就立刻有什么东西告诉我这是不对的。但是，是的，现在精神在帮助我，帮助我，我一下子就拥有了它，并写道：
